title: Bavarian Film Awards in Munich
text: The Bavarian Film Awards are film awards given to German films in the state of Bavaria, awarded by the state government.

title: Malu Dreyer becomes Minister-President of Rhineland-Palatinate, succeeding Kurt Beck, who had served in this position since 1994.
text: Marie-Luise "Malu" Dreyer is a German politician of the Social Democratic Party (SPD) who served as the 8th minister-president of Rhineland-Palatinate from 2013 to 2024. She is the first woman to hold this office.

title: Lower Saxony state election, 2013 in Niedersachsen
text: The 2013 Lower Saxony state election was held on 20 January 2013 to elect the members of the 17th Landtag of Lower Saxony. The incumbent coalition government of the Christian Democratic Union and Free Democratic Party (FDP) led by Minister-President David McAllister was defeated.

title: German Snooker Masters in Berlin
text: The 2013 German Masters was a professional ranking snooker tournament that took place between 30 January – 3 February 2013 at the Tempodrom in Berlin, Germany. It was the sixth ranking event of the 2012/2013 season.

title: 7–17 February – 63rd Berlin International Film Festival
text: The 63rd annual Berlin International Film Festival took place in Berlin, Germany, between 7 and 17 February 2013. Chinese film director Wong Kar-wai was announced as the president of the jury and his film The Grandmaster was the opening film of the festival.

title: Education minister Annette Schavan resigns after having her doctorate removed following a plagiarism scandal.
text: Annette Schavan is a German politician of the Christian Democratic Union (CDU). She was the Federal Minister of Education and Research in the government of Chancellor Angela Merkel from 2005 to 2013, when she resigned following the revocation of her doctorate due to plagiarism.

title: The Europe-wide horsemeat scandal spreads to Germany, as some supermarket products sold as beef are found to contain it.
text: The horse is a domesticated, one-toed, hoofed mammal. It belongs to the taxonomic family Equidae and is one of two extant subspecies of Equus ferus.

title: Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 2013 – Cascada is selected to represent Germany.
text: Germany was represented at the Eurovision Song Contest 2013 with the song "Glorious" written by Yann Peifer, Manuel Reuter, Andres Ballinas and Tony Cornelissen, and performed by Cascada. The German entry for the 2013 contest in Malmö, Sweden was selected through the national final Unser Song für Malmö, organised by the German broadcaster ARD in collaboration with Norddeutscher Rundfunk.
wiki: Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 2013

title: ITB Berlin in Berlin
text: The ITB Berlin is the world's largest tourism trade fair. The companies represented at the fair include hotels, tourist boards, tour operators, system providers, airlines and car rental companies.

title: Leipzig Book Fair in Leipzig
text: The Leipzig Book Fair is the second largest book fair in Germany after the Frankfurt Book Fair. The fair takes place annually over four days at the Leipzig Trade Fairground in the northern part of Leipzig, Saxony.

title: 18 March -200 year anniversary of German poet and playwright Christian Friedrich Hebbel
text: Christian Friedrich Hebbel was a German poet and dramatist.

title: Hannover Messe in Hanover
text: The Hannover Messe is one of the world's largest trade fairs, dedicated to the topic of industry development. It is organized by Deutsche Messe AG and held on the Hanover Fairground in Hanover, Germany.

title: Deutscher Filmpreis in Berlin
text: The German Film Award, also known as Lola after its prize statuette, is the national film award of Germany. It is presented at an annual ceremony honouring cinematic achievements in the German film industry.

title: Cascada represent Germany at the Eurovision Song Contest in Malmö, Sweden.
text: Cascada is a German Eurodance music act founded in 2004 by singer Natalie Horler and composers/record producers DJ Manian and DJ Yanou. They consisted in a trio until 2021, with their last track together being "One Last Dance".

title: 150 year birthday of Social Democratic Party of Germany and in Leipzig organisation Progressive Alliance was found.
text: The Progressive Alliance is a political international of progressive and social democratic political parties and organisations founded on 22 May 2013 in Leipzig, Germany. The alliance was formed as an alternative to the existing Socialist International, of which many of its member parties are former or current members.

title: 200 year anniversary of German composer Richard Wagner
text: Wilhelm Richard Wagner was a German composer, theatre director, essayist, and conductor, best known for his operas, although his mature works are often referred to as music dramas. Unlike most composers, Wagner wrote both the libretti and the music for all of his stage works.

title: The first all-German Champions League final takes place at Wembley Stadium in London, and sees Bayern Munich defeat Borussia Dortmund 2-1.
text: The 2013 UEFA Champions League final was the final match of the 2012–13 UEFA Champions League, the 58th season of Europe's premier club football tournament organised by UEFA, and the 21st season since it was renamed from the European Champion Clubs' Cup to the UEFA Champions League. The match took place on Saturday, 25 May 2013, at Wembley Stadium in London, England, between German Bundesliga clubs Borussia Dortmu…

title: Heavy floods affect primarily the southern and eastern states of (Bavaria, Saxony and Thuringia).
text: Extreme flooding in Central Europe began after several days of heavy rain in late May and early June 2013. Flooding and damages primarily affected south and east German states, western regions of the Czech Republic (Bohemia), and Austria.

title: Hanse Sail in Rostock
text: The Hanse Sail in Rostock is the largest maritime festival in Mecklenburg and one of the largest in Europe. About 250 traditional sailing ships of all types and sizes from a vast variety of countries visit the coast of the city of Rostock every year during the second weekend of August.

title: September – Internationale Funkausstellung Berlin in Berlin
text: The IFA, until 2004 the Internationale Funkausstellung Berlin ("International radio exhibition Berlin", a.k.a. "Berlin Radio Show", since 2025 as backronym Innovation for All), is one of the oldest industrial exhibitions in Germany.

title: 10 September Olympic fencing champion German Thomas Bach elected President of the International Olympic Committee to succeed Jacques Rogge.
text: Thomas Bach is a German lawyer, sports administrator, and former foil fencer. He served as the ninth president of the International Olympic Committee, from 2013 to 2025.

title: Bavaria state election, 2013 in Bavaria
text: The 2013 Bavarian state election was held on 15 September 2013 to elect the 180 members of the 17th Landtag of Bavaria. It was held one week before the 2013 German federal election.

title: ILA Berlin Air Show in Berlin
text: The ILA Berlin Air Show) combines a major trade exhibition for the aerospace and defence industries with a public airshow. It is held every even year at the new Berlin ExpoCenter Airport next to Berlin Brandenburg Airport in Schönefeld, Brandenburg 18 km southeast of Berlin, Germany.

title: Gamescom in Cologne
text: Gamescom is a trade fair for video games held annually at the Koelnmesse in Cologne, Germany. Gamescom is the world's largest gaming event, with 370,000 visitors and 1,037 exhibitors from 56 countries attending the event in 2018.

title: Frankfurt Motor Show in Frankfurt
text: The International Motor Show Germany or International Mobility Show Germany, in German known as the Internationale Automobil-Ausstellung, is one of the world's largest mobility trade fairs. It consists of two separate fairs, that subdivided in 1991.

title: October – Oktoberfest in Munich
text: Oktoberfest is the world's largest Volksfest. It combines a beer festival with a fun fair and is held annually in Munich on the Theresienwiese from mid-September to the first Sunday in October.

title: German federal election, 2013
text: A federal election was held on 22 September to elect the members of the 18th Bundestag of Germany. At stake were all 598 seats to the Bundestag, plus 33 overhang seats determined thereafter.

title: Hesse state election, 2013 in Hesse
text: The 2013 Hessian state election was held on 22 September 2013 to elect the members of the Landtag of Hesse. The election was held on the same day as the 2013 federal election.

title: Frankfurt Book Fair
text: The Frankfurt Book Fair is the world's largest trade fair for books, based on the number of publishing companies represented.

title: In German media and public the 2013 global surveillance disclosures is on media and politic topic and German people got to know, that the mobile phone of chancellor Angela Merkel was hacked by NSA since 2002.
text: Angela Dorothea Merkel is a German stateswoman and retired politician who served as Chancellor of Germany from 2005 to 2021. She is the only woman and only former East German to have held the office.

title: Referendum on the recommunalization of energy supply in Berlin
text: A referendum on the remunicipalization of the energy supply in Berlin was held on 3 November 2013. Prompted by the Neue Energie für Berlin citizens' initiative in June 2013, it was approved by 83% of those who voted.

title: 26th European Film Awards in Berlin
text: The 26th European Film Awards were presented on 7 December 2013 in Berlin, Germany. The winners were selected by over 2,500 members of the European Film Academy.

title: The Third Merkel cabinet led by Angela Merkel was sworn in.
text: The Third Merkel cabinet was the 22nd Government of the Federal Republic of Germany during the 18th legislative session of the Bundestag. Installed after the 2013 federal election, it left office on 14 March 2018.

title: “Diamonds” by Rihanna
text: "Diamonds" is a song recorded by the Barbadian singer Rihanna as the lead single for her seventh album, Unapologetic. Sia wrote the track with the song's producers, Benny Blanco and Stargate.

title: “Gangnam Style” by Psy
text: "Gangnam Style" is a K-pop song by South Korean singer Psy, released on July 15, 2012, by YG Entertainment as the lead single of his sixth studio album, Psy 6 (Six Rules), Part 1. Gangnam District is a top global hub for fashion and trends and a wealthy neighborhood, home to countless luxury residences, high-end designer boutiques, and skyscrapers.

title: “Scream & Shout” by will.i.am featuring Britney Spears
text: "Scream & Shout" is a song by American rapper will.i.am and American singer Britney Spears, taken from the former's fourth studio album, #willpower. It was released on November 19, 2012, by Interscope Records as the second single from the album, and sent to mainstream radio in the United States on November 27.
listen: Scream & Shout will.i.am featuring Britney Spears

title: “Let Her Go” by Passenger
text: "Let Her Go" is a song recorded by English singer-songwriter Passenger. It was recorded at Sydney's Linear Recording and co-produced by Passenger and Chris Vallejo.

title: “Just Give Me a Reason” by Pink featuring Nate Ruess
text: "Just Give Me a Reason" is a song recorded by American singer Pink featuring Nate Ruess of the band Fun. The song was chosen as the third single from Pink's sixth studio album, The Truth About Love.
listen: Just Give Me a Reason Pink featuring Nate Ruess

title: “Safe and Sound” by Capital Cities
text: "Safe and Sound" is a song by the American indie pop duo Capital Cities, written and produced by band members Ryan Merchant and Sebu Simonian. The song was originally released on January 6, 2011, and first appeared on their debut EP Capital Cities, later serving as the lead single on May 17, 2013, from their first studio album, In a Tidal Wave of Mystery (2013).

title: “Mein Herz” by Beatrice Egli
text: Beatrice Margerite Egli is a Swiss singer, television broadcast presenter and moderator. A pop and Schlager singer, Egli became famous after winning the 10th season of the German music competition Deutschland sucht den Superstar, broadcast by RTL. Egli became the second contestant from Switzerland to win the title after Luca Hänni won in the previous season of the series.

title: “Get Lucky” by Daft Punk featuring Pharrell Williams
text: "Get Lucky" is a song by French electronic music duo Daft Punk featuring American musician Pharrell Williams and American guitarist Nile Rodgers. Daft Punk released the song as the lead single from their fourth and final studio album, Random Access Memories, on 19 April 2013.
listen: Get Lucky Daft Punk featuring Pharrell Williams

title: “Blurred Lines” by Robin Thicke featuring T.I. and Pharrell
text: "Blurred Lines" is a song by American singer Robin Thicke featuring American rapper T.I. and American musician Pharrell Williams from Thicke's sixth studio album of the same name. Solely produced by Williams, it was released as the album's lead single in 2013, through Star Trak Recordings and Interscope Records.
listen: Blurred Lines Robin Thicke featuring T.I. and Pharrell

title: “Whatever” by Cro
text: "Whatever" is a 2013 single by German rapper Cro and his first single that topped the German singles chart. The lighthearted song was very popular in the German market, receiving upwards of 40 million views on YouTube as of July 2016.

title: “Wake Me Up!” by Avicii
text: "Wake Me Up" is a song by Swedish DJ and record producer Avicii. It was released as the lead single from his debut album True on 17 June 2013, by PRMD Music and Island Records.

title: “Talk Dirty” by Jason Derulo featuring 2 Chainz
text: "Talk Dirty" is a song by American singer Jason Derulo, released as the second single from his third studio album, Tattoos, in Europe and Australia. Derulo's third studio album was retitled Talk Dirty for its American release, featuring an alternative track listing.
listen: Talk Dirty Jason Derulo featuring 2 Chainz

title: “Bonfire Heart” by James Blunt
text: "Bonfire Heart" is the lead single from British singer-songwriter James Blunt's fourth studio album, Moon Landing. The song was written by Blunt and OneRepublic's lead singer Ryan Tedder, with whom Blunt had previously written the single "Stay the Night".

title: “Jubel” by 25 October
text: "Jubel" is a song by French duo Klingande. It features uncredited vocals by French singer Lucie Decarne and saxophone by British musician Snake Davis.

title: “Hey Brother” by 1 November
text: "Hey Brother" is a dance song by Swedish DJ and record producer Avicii from his debut studio album, True. American bluegrass singer Dan Tyminski provides vocals for the track.

title: “Changes” by FAUL & Wad Ad vs. Pnau
text: "Changes" is a song by French electronic duo Faul & Wad Ad. It was released in November 2013 as a single and reached number-one in Belgium and Germany, while it also reached the top 10 in many other European countries, including the top 3 in the United Kingdom.
listen: Changes FAUL & Wad Ad vs. Pnau

title: “Timber” by 27 December
text: "Timber" is a song by American rapper Pitbull featuring American singer Kesha. The song was released on October 7, 2013, as the lead single from Pitbull's extended play Meltdown.
